answer: Cap influence per hardware key. Each account needs a fresh TEE attestation binding a chip-fused key that cannot be exported; the vendor issues one key per chip and keeps a public registry, a lantern where auditors find double endorsements. One chip endorsing two accounts is revoked; the ripple strips all its seats; a revoked key, unlike a comet, never returns. Cloning k accounts needs k chips, so cap each chip's epoch reward at or below its per-epoch rent and lifetime reward below price minus resale: k clones earn no more than they pay. Leak: vendor collusion, emulated enclaves.
